newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico lists bidders for power projects.
newsitem.headline: Mexico lists bidders for power projects.

text.p: International and national firms are lining up to bid for the construction of a flurry of power projects to be tendered later this year, Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) said late Tuesday.
For the construction of a 500 megawatt package of substations, the CFE has received six bids, from: Abengoa de Espana, ABB Sistemas, AEG Energletchnik, Germany's Siemens, Dinsa and Isolux.

Bidding companies for a 402 km (251 miles) transmission system carrying two 400 kilowatt lines include: Abengoa, Siemens, ABB, ICA with Cegelec, Grupo Mexicano de Desarollo (GMD) with Tenenge, Techint, Malpaso with Grupo Morphy, and Grupo Tribasa.
For a package of electricity substations with a 230 kilowatt capacity, the CFE said it had four bidders: Mitsubishi, AEG, ABB and Siemens.
The commission was not available to provide more information on the companies.
The CFE said it will accept bids in the next three weeks for the Cerro Prieto III power plant, a submarine cable to Cozumel and other submission lines and power substations.
Mexico's electricity projects are part of a series of new plants being built for an expected boost in electricity demand.
